review_notes: I read the whole target file, then Conjugation.lean in full. I grepped for other uses of smulRight/dualTensorHom-based tensor induction and for imports of Cyclicity. BaseChange.lean uses a similar induction, but it is not derivable from cyclicity, so I did not report it. The two `sub_eq_add_neg, map_add` steps in the commutator proof are short calculations, so I did not report them. I could not run Lean, so the proposed rewrite of traceOfFiniteProjective_conj is untested. It needs Conjugation.lean to import Cyclicity. Cyclicity imports only Basic, and Trace.lean imports both, so I found no cycle. The `comp_assoc`/`symm_comp_self` rewriting steps may need adjustment.

findings.excerpt: obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := (dualTensorHom_bijective (R := R) (M := M) (N := N)).2 f
findings.problem: Two proofs repeat the same machinery. Each takes a surjection from the dual tensor product (`dualTensorHom_bijective`) and inducts with `TensorProduct.inductionOn`. In the `tmul` case each proves, by `ext` and `map_smul`, that composing a rank-one map `dualTensorHom (φ ⊗ y)` with a linear map gives another `smulRight`. The `add` case is closed by `simp only [map_add, ...]`. Cyclicity does this at lines 51–67 (`h₁ : g.comp (dualTensorHom ...) = φ.smulRight (g y)`). `traceOfFiniteProjective_conj` in Conjugation.lean does it again for `e.conj (dualTensorHom ...) = (φ.comp e.symm).smulRight (e x)`. Conjugation invariance is a special case of cyclicity, because `e.conj f = (e.comp f).comp e.symm`. So the second tensor-induction proof is redundant.
findings.proposed_change: Keep `traceOfFiniteProjective_comp_comm` as the only place that does the rank-one reduction. Make Conjugation.lean import `ProjectiveModules.Module.Trace.Cyclicity` and replace the proof of `traceOfFiniteProjective_conj` with a short derivation. Rewrite `LinearEquiv.conj_apply` to get `((↑e).comp f).comp (e.symm : N →ₗ[R] M)`. Apply `traceOfFiniteProjective_comp_comm R M N (e : M →ₗ[R] N) (f.comp e.symm)`. This gives `trace_M ((f.comp e.symm).comp e) = trace_N (e.comp (f.comp e.symm))`. Then use `LinearMap.comp_assoc` and `e.symm_comp_self`-style lemmas (`LinearEquiv.symm_comp_self` or equivalent; I did not check the exact name) to reduce the left side to `f` and the right side to `e.conj f`. Cyclicity itself is unchanged. The unchanged theorem is the shared lemma, and the conjugation proof loses its own `obtain`, `induction`, `h`, and `add` branch.
findings.benefit: The tensor-induction argument, which is the only nontrivial part, lives in one theorem. Conjugation invariance becomes an explicit corollary of cyclicity, so the file structure shows the real dependency. Maintainers change one induction instead of two near-copies. The downstream client `FiniteProjectiveTracePiNonfreeClient` imports both files, so the new import adds no dependency problem.
